symptoms.question: Does the engine misfire or run rough mainly at idle? (yes/no)
Are misfires worse in wet or humid weather? (yes/no)
Do you hear popping/backfiring through the intake when starting or accelerating? (yes/no)
Does the engine crank normally but fail to start? (yes/no)

rules.diagnosis: Misfire at idle with a check engine light often points to ignition coil or spark plug issues.
rules.advice: Continued misfiring can damage the catalytic converter. Have ignition components and fault codes checked.

rules.diagnosis: Misfires that are worse in wet weather suggest moisture-sensitive ignition leads or coil packs.
rules.advice: Inspect ignition leads and coils for cracks and moisture paths and consider replacement.

rules.diagnosis: Backfiring through the intake can be caused by incorrect ignition timing or lean misfire.
rules.advice: Driving should be limited until ignition timing and air–fuel mixture have been checked.

rules.diagnosis: Strong fuel smell with cranking but no start suggests lack of spark rather than fuel.
rules.advice: Have the ignition system checked for spark at the plugs and possible crankshaft or camshaft sensor faults.

rules.diagnosis: Misfire and hesitation mainly under load with a check engine light, without black smoke or fuel smell, often indicates ignition weakness under load (coil, plugs, leads).
rules.advice: Avoid heavy acceleration and have ignition components and fault codes checked. Misfires under load can worsen and may damage the catalytic converter.
